title: The Trick To Making Your Online Lessons Less Boring s-boring/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies a single, simple fix for the flatness of online instruction: stand up. Rather than sitting behind a laptop with a static screen share, he urges teachers to use an easel or whiteboard and physically move, gesture, and perform the way they would in person, arguing this eliminates the 'talking-head' droning that makes remote lessons feel indistinguishable from passive video consumption. He points to teachers succeeding online as those minimizing screen shares in favor of direct camera engagement, physical demonstration, and even theatrical embodiment of characters and content. The piece frames standing up as merely the starting move — the fuller shift is letting go of self-consciousness and fear entirely to teach with full physical commitment despite the limitations of a screen.
points: Standing up rather than sitting behind a screen share is offered as the single simplest fix for flat, disengaging online lessons.
Physical movement and gesture are said to force greater energy and demonstrativeness, pulling students out of passive viewing mode.
Successful online teachers are described as minimizing screen shares and doc-cams in favor of direct camera engagement.
Physically embodying characters and content, even theatrically, is cited as a way to bring curriculum to life despite screen limitations.
The fuller shift recommended is letting go of self-consciousness entirely, not just standing up as a one-time technique.
quotes: Learning online is b-o-r-i-n-g, especially because students associate screen time with immersive content—video games, Netflix, social media, YouTube.
It’s to drag out that old, beat-up easel or portable whiteboard and teach like you’re in person . Do this and your students will forget they’re even online.
It eliminates the talking-head syndrome, the droning, and the same old same old of laptop schooling.
The few teachers who are managing to keep their students attentive during the pandemic are those who are opening up and sharing what is happening in their own space.
It starts with pushing your chair away and standing up. Do this and you’ll become a better, more effective teacher immediately.
